david_customer: Hey team — after the 2026-03-16 rollout our app is getting wrong completions for some users. Examples attached. Seems like outputs are coming from an older policy/model for requests that include a certain prefix.

alice_support: Sorry about that, can you paste a minimal repro (input + X-Req-Id) and the time you saw it? Also which region?

david_customer: Repro below — seen in us-east-1 at 17:14 UTC. Request id X-Req-Id: r-0a1b2c3d. Input: 
```
{"prompt":"Summarize user message: [ORDER #1234] I changed my plan...","model":"redwood-3b-v1","user_id":"acct-77"}
```
Response we got (wrong): "Your billing remains on legacy plan X" — should reference the new billing verbiage.

deploy-bot: Deployment finished: rollout redwood-rewrite-prefix-hash commit sha:aa11bbcc at 2026-03-16T16:50:12Z — canary 10% -> 100% after 20m. :rocket:

alice_support: tagging infra/eng. @brian_engineer @carmen_oncall — customer provided request id.

brian_engineer: I saw this in telemetry — a spike in "stale-output" alerts right after the deploy. Looks like the change to prefix key hashing (we replaced sha1 with cityhash32 to shave latency) changed key namespaces for prefix cache entries. If some requests still reference the old key shape they could be hitting stale KV entries that weren't invalidated.

carmen_oncall: Confirming — I ran a quick scan of the redis instance used for us-east-1 prefix cache (cache-prod-redis-3). Found two patterns: old keys like `prefix:sha1:<model>:<prefix-hash>` and new keys like `prefix:city32:<model>:<prefix-hash>`. TTLs on some old keys are still long (7d).

carmen_oncall: Commands I ran: 
```
# list a few sample keys
redis-cli -h cache-prod-redis-3 --scan --pattern 'prefix:sha1:*' | head -n 10
redis-cli -h cache-prod-redis-3 TTL prefix:sha1:redwood-3b-v1:abcd1234
```

brian_engineer: That matches my theory. We expected a migration that would populate new keys on cache miss, but because the service used mixed key encoders during the canary (some workers built with old binary, some with new) a fraction of requests wrote old-key entries while the majority read new keys — producing cross-key collisions and apparent stale outputs when a read hit an old entry for a different model/prompt variation.

alice_support: What's the immediate customer-facing mitigation? They are seeing wrong outputs in production.

brian_engineer: Short term: purge the old-key namespace so all reads go to new-key path. Two options: 1) run a namespace delete for `prefix:sha1:*` in the affected Redis shards (fast but irreversible), or 2) enable a runtime flag to turn caching off for prefix lookups (safe, higher cost).

carmen_oncall: I'm going to prepare the purge commands but will wait for approval. Purge command (example):
```
# careful, this deletes all sha1 prefix keys in that shard
redis-cli -h cache-prod-redis-3 --scan --pattern 'prefix:sha1:*' | xargs -n 100 redis-cli -h cache-prod-redis-3 DEL
```

alice_support: @david_customer we can do a purge now or toggle caching off while we validate. Which would you prefer? Purge has brief risk window, toggle increases latency for a few minutes.

david_customer: Please purge — the wrong outputs are a high-severity business impact for us. We prefer a fast fix.

brian_engineer: Ok preparing PR to add a migration that writes both key styles for 48h to avoid this in future and a follow-up to ensure consistent encoder versions during canary. Also adding a healthcheck that alerts if mixed key namespaces are observed.

carmen_oncall: Performing purge on shard-3 now (following runbook). I'll sequence across shards and post status. :hourglass: 

cachebot: Purge started on cache-prod-redis-3 by carmen_oncall at 2026-03-16T17:05:08Z. Deleting 24,132 keys (estimated).

carmen_oncall: Shard-3 purge complete. Running post-purge verification: sample request r-0a1b2c3d re-run at 17:11 UTC returned correct verbiage.

david_customer: Confirmed — our downstream now seeing correct billing message. Thank you. :pray:

brian_engineer: Root cause summary for postmortem: accidental mixed key encoder deployment during canary + long TTLs on old-key namespace. Fixes: 1) purge old keys (done), 2) migration path to write dual keys for 48h (PR open), 3) reduce TTL on prefix cache to 1h for 7-day window during migrations, 4) add canary gating that detects divergent cache key namespaces.

alice_support: Thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread for follow-ups. @brian_engineer please add a short incident blurb to postmortems/ with timeline and customer impact.

brian_engineer: Will do — linking the incident ticket INC-2026-1823 and the PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/742

carmen_oncall: Closing oncall tasks. If anyone sees repeat reports, re-open thread.

david_customer: Appreciate the quick turnaround.

alice_support: Marking resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
